findings.cross_file_justification: The new rule reroutes archive, ledger and decisions merges from the `Prepare Release (Cycle)` job to the `Prepare Release (Bugfix or Other)` job in `.github/workflows/post-merge.yml`. This file's own documentation describes the `other` route as "tag only" (header, line 28) and the R-005 comment (lines 85-91) records that `other` -> "simple-release path -> conventional PATCH auto-tag" produced the wrong tag v1.195.1 on PR #1201. The triage asserts the Bugfix-or-Other path "prepares nothing release-worthy for an unchanged CHANGELOG", but neither the diff nor the implementer report shows what that job does for `pr_type=other` with a PR number, and the only existing evidence that `other` is inert (the ledger push, KF063-T1) is the no-PR shape, which the workflow may gate separately.
findings.description: The fix changes which post-merge job runs for `chore/` merges, but the behaviour of the destination route is asserted, not evidenced. Two shapes matter: (a) a chore-only archive merge with an unchanged CHANGELOG; (b) a `chore/` branch merge that contains `fix:` commits, e.g. the PR #1295 shape (`chore/cycle-133-post-ship`), which the implementer confirms now routes `other` as well. If the simple-release path still performs the conventional-commit PATCH auto-tag described in the R-005 comment, shape (b) trades an unpublished spurious candidate (today's symptom) for an actual spurious tag, which is harder to undo (R-005 needed a manual delete+retag).
findings.failure_mode: A `chore/` branch merge carrying any `fix:` commit now takes the simple-release path; if that path auto-tags on conventional commits, the repo receives an unintended PATCH tag on a housekeeping merge, which is a worse outcome than the unpublished candidate this fix removes.
findings.suggested_fix: Before landing, read the `Prepare Release (Bugfix or Other)` job and the orchestrator's simple-release branch (or dry-run them) for `pr_type=other` with a PR number, once with chore-only commits and once with a `fix:` commit present. If the path tags, gate the auto-tag on `pr_type == 'bugfix'` or on a non-empty CHANGELOG `[Unreleased]`. Record the result in reviewer.md as the E2E, and correct the stale "(tag only)" wording at line 28 so the header matches the actual route semantics.
findings.failure_scenario: A `chore/` branch merge carrying any `fix:` commit now takes the simple-release path; if that path auto-tags on conventional commits, the repo receives an unintended PATCH tag on a housekeeping merge, which is a worse outcome than the unpublished candidate this fix removes.

findings.description: The prefix clause is `^chore\((archive|ledger|decisions)\):`, not the triage/sprint form `^chore(\([^)]*\))?:`. The narrowing is well justified (the pinned case at tests/unit/post-merge-classifier.bats:120-124 expects `chore: cycle-042 release prep ...` -> `cycle`, and PR #747 `chore(release): ... (cycle-098 ...)` is a real named release), but it leaves the triage's stated Expected Behavior ("a subject with the conventional `chore:` / `chore(scope):` prefix ... must take the Bugfix or Other path") unmet for two live shapes: `chore: ... cycle-NNN ...` and `chore(cycle-NNN): ...`. The implementer counts 40+ historical `chore(cycle-NNN): RESUMPTION.md ...` squash merges; each of those is a PR merge (squash implies a PR trailer) that still classifies `cycle` and would still run the full pipeline and prepare a spurious candidate, the same incident class as bd-ahxmh.
findings.failure_mode: If any tool or operator still produces `chore(cycle-NNN): ...` PR squash merges, the bead is closed while that shape continues to prepare spurious cycle candidates, and the triage's expected-behaviour text no longer describes the shipped contract, inviting a later reviewer to "fix" the regex back to the bare form and reopen the PR #747 release hole.
findings.suggested_fix: Amend the bead/triage Expected Behavior and header rule 1a to state the narrowed contract explicitly, including that `chore:` and `chore(release):` naming a cycle stay `cycle` by design. Check whether `chore(cycle-NNN):` subjects are still emitted anywhere (RESUMPTION.md tooling); if so, add `cycle-[0-9]+` to the scope alternation with a pinned PCT case, otherwise file a follow-up bead so the partial coverage is tracked.
findings.failure_scenario: If any tool or operator still produces `chore(cycle-NNN): ...` PR squash merges, the bead is closed while that shape continues to prepare spurious cycle candidates, and the triage's expected-behaviour text no longer describes the shipped contract, inviting a later reviewer to "fix" the regex back to the bare form and reopen the PR #747 release hole.

findings.description: The diff edits a System Zone file but contains no `checksums.json` or `REPO-MAP.md` update. The sprint acceptance criteria require the manifests to be regenerated in the same commit and `tools/gen-checksums.sh --check`, `tools/check-manifest-paths.sh` and `repo-map-gen.sh --validate` to pass; the DEC-0824 bounded-marker placement of the edit is also not evidenced in the report. The implementer explicitly handed these to the lead, so this is a merge gate rather than a missed item.
findings.failure_mode: If the fix commit lands as diffed, the recorded checksum for classify-pr-type.sh is stale: the System Zone integrity check fails in CI or a hook and blocks the merge, or, if the check is not enforced on this path, the manifest silently drifts from the file it is supposed to pin.
findings.suggested_fix: In the fix commit (not the red commit), regenerate `checksums.json` and `REPO-MAP.md`, then run `tools/gen-checksums.sh --check`, `tools/check-manifest-paths.sh` and `repo-map-gen.sh --validate`; confirm the new rule sits inside the DEC-0824 bounded marker region and record all three results in reviewer.md.
findings.failure_scenario: If the fix commit lands as diffed, the recorded checksum for classify-pr-type.sh is stale: the System Zone integrity check fails in CI or a hook and blocks the merge, or, if the check is not enforced on this path, the manifest silently drifts from the file it is supposed to pin.
